questions.prompt: For \(\vec{v}(t)=5t\hat{\imath}-2t^2\hat{\jmath}\), find \(\vec{a}(t)\).
For \(\vec{r}(t)=t^3\hat{\imath}+2t^2\hat{\jmath}\), find \(\vec{a}(t)\).
If \(a_x=0\) but \(a_y\neq0\), can the path curve?
questions.answer: Yes. A transverse acceleration component changes the velocity direction, so the path can curve.

questions.prompt: Find the magnitude of \(\vec{a}=3\hat{\imath}+4\hat{\jmath}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\).
A particle's velocity changes from \(2\hat{\imath}+3\hat{\jmath}\) to \(10\hat{\imath}-1\hat{\jmath}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) in \(4\,\mathrm{s}\). Find average acceleration.
For \(\vec{v}=t^2\hat{\imath}+t^2\hat{\jmath}\), find \(\vec{a}\) and its direction at \(t=1\,\mathrm{s}\).
questions.answer:
\[
\vec{a}=2t\hat{\imath}+2t\hat{\jmath}
\]
\[
\vec{a}(1)=2\hat{\imath}+2\hat{\jmath}
\]
The direction is \(45^\circ\) above \(+\hat{\imath}\).

questions.prompt: For \(\vec{r}(t)=4t\hat{\imath}+7\hat{\jmath}\), find \(\vec{a}\).
questions.answer:
\[
\vec{v}=4\hat{\imath}
\]
\[
\vec{a}=0
\]

questions.prompt: Can an object have acceleration when its speed is constant?
questions.answer: Yes. If direction changes, velocity changes. Uniform circular motion has constant speed but nonzero inward acceleration.

questions.prompt: If \(\vec{a}=0\), what can be said about \(\vec{v}\)?
questions.answer: The velocity vector is constant. Both speed and direction stay fixed.

questions.prompt: A particle has \(\vec{v}=4\hat{\imath}+3\hat{\jmath}\) and \(\vec{a}=3\hat{\imath}-4\hat{\jmath}\). Is its speed changing at that instant?
questions.answer:
Check the dot product:
\[
\vec{v}\cdot\vec{a}=4(3)+3(-4)=0
\]
The acceleration is perpendicular to velocity, so speed is not changing at that instant.

questions.prompt: For \(\vec{v}=3\hat{\imath}+4t\hat{\jmath}+5t^2\hat{k}\), find \(\vec{a}\) at \(t=2\,\mathrm{s}\).
For \(\vec{v}=6\hat{\imath}\) and \(\vec{a}=-2\hat{\imath}\), is speed increasing or decreasing?
questions.answer: Velocity and acceleration point in opposite directions, so the speed is decreasing.

questions.prompt: For \(\vec{r}(t)=t^2\hat{\imath}-4t\hat{\jmath}+9\hat{k}\), find \(\vec{a}\).
For \(\vec{a}=6t\hat{\imath}\) and \(\vec{v}(0)=2\hat{\imath}+3\hat{\jmath}\), find \(\vec{v}(t)\).
questions.answer:
\[
\vec{v}(t)=\vec{v}(0)+\int_0^t6\tau\hat{\imath}\,d\tau
\]
\[
\vec{v}(t)=(2+3t^2)\hat{\imath}+3\hat{\jmath}
\]

questions.prompt: For \(\vec{v}=-6\hat{\imath}\) and \(\vec{a}=-2\hat{\imath}\), is speed increasing or decreasing? Justify with \(d|\vec v|/dt\).
questions.answer:
\[
\frac{d|\vec v|}{dt}=\frac{\vec v\cdot\vec a}{|\vec v|}
\]
\[
\vec v\cdot\vec a=(-6)(-2)=12>0
\]
So speed is increasing.

questions.prompt: For \(\vec{r}(t)=\cos t\,\hat{\imath}+\sin t\,\hat{\jmath}\), find \(\vec{a}(t)\).
A velocity vector rotates while keeping the same magnitude. Is acceleration zero?
questions.answer: No. A changing direction means the velocity vector changes, so acceleration is nonzero.

questions.prompt: A particle has \(\vec v=(2t)\hat{\imath}+(t^2-4)\hat{\jmath}\). Find all \(t\) for which speed is stationary \((d|\vec v|/dt=0)\).
questions.answer:
Speed is stationary when
\[
\frac{d}{dt}(|\vec v|^2)=2\vec v\cdot\vec a=0
\]
\[
\vec v=(2t)\hat\imath+(t^2-4)\hat\jmath,
\quad
\vec a=2\hat\imath+2t\hat\jmath
\]
\[
\vec v\cdot\vec a=4t+2t(t^2-4)=2t^3-4t=2t(t^2-2)
\]
\[
t=0,\ \pm\sqrt2
\]

questions.prompt: A particle has constant \(\vec a=2\hat{\imath}-3\hat{\jmath}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\) and \(\vec v(0)=4\hat{\imath}+\hat{\jmath}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the first time when \(\vec v\) is perpendicular to \(\vec a\).
questions.answer:
\[
\vec v(t)=\vec v(0)+\vec a t=(4+2t)\hat\imath+(1-3t)\hat\jmath
\]
Require \(\vec v\cdot\vec a=0\):
\[
(4+2t)(2)+(1-3t)(-3)=0
\]
\[
8+4t-3+9t=0
\Rightarrow 13t+5=0
\Rightarrow t=-\frac{5}{13}\,\mathrm s
\]
No positive-time solution exists, so after \(t=0\) velocity never becomes perpendicular to \(\vec a\).

questions.prompt: For \(\vec{v}=2t\hat{\imath}-t\hat{\jmath}+4\hat{k}\), find \(\vec{a}\), and compute tangential acceleration \(a_t\) at \(t=1\).
questions.answer:
\[
\vec a=2\hat\imath-\hat\jmath
\]
At \(t=1\):
\[
\vec v(1)=2\hat\imath-\hat\jmath+4\hat k,
\quad
|\vec v(1)|=\sqrt{21}
\]
Tangential acceleration:
\[
a_t=\frac{\vec v\cdot\vec a}{|\vec v|}
=\frac{(2)(2)+(-1)(-1)+4(0)}{\sqrt{21}}
=\frac{5}{\sqrt{21}}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}
\]

questions.prompt: For \(\vec{r}(t)=R\cos(\omega t)\hat{\imath}+R\sin(\omega t)\hat{\jmath}\), derive \(a_t\), \(a_n\), and prove \(|\vec a|=\omega^2R\) even though \(\vec a\) changes direction.
questions.answer:
\[
\vec v=-R\omega\sin(\omega t)\hat\imath+R\omega\cos(\omega t)\hat\jmath,
\quad |\vec v|=R\omega
\]
\[
\vec a=-R\omega^2\cos(\omega t)\hat\imath-R\omega^2\sin(\omega t)\hat\jmath
\]
Tangential component:
\[
a_t=\frac{d|\vec v|}{dt}=0
\]
Normal component:
\[
a_n=\frac{|\vec v|^2}{R}=\frac{(R\omega)^2}{R}=R\omega^2
\]
So
\[
|\vec a|=\sqrt{a_t^2+a_n^2}=R\omega^2
\]
constant in magnitude, while direction rotates inward with the radius.

questions.prompt: A particle moves in a plane with \(\vec a=-\lambda\vec v+\beta\,\hat{k}\times\vec v\), where \(\lambda,\beta>0\) constants. Derive \(d|\vec v|/dt\), then state and justify whether speed can increase at any time.
questions.answer:
Given
\[
\vec a=-\lambda\vec v+\beta(\hat k\times\vec v)
\]
take dot product with \(\vec v\):
\[
\vec v\cdot\vec a=-\lambda|\vec v|^2+\beta\,\vec v\cdot(\hat k\times\vec v)
\]
But \(\vec v\cdot(\hat k\times\vec v)=0\), so
\[
\vec v\cdot\vec a=-\lambda|\vec v|^2
\]
Hence
\[
\frac{d|\vec v|}{dt}=\frac{\vec v\cdot\vec a}{|\vec v|}=-\lambda|\vec v|\le0
\]
Speed cannot increase; it decays exponentially unless \(|\vec v|=0\). The \(\beta\)-term only rotates \(\vec v\).
